title: Liberia agrees to take 1,200 third-country deportees from the U.S.
summary:
Liberia agrees to take 1,200 third-country deportees from the U.S.toggle caption Angelina Katsanis/AP PhotoMONROVIA, Liberia — Liberia has agreed to accept up to 1,200 third-country deportees from the United States, authorities in the West African country said Tuesday, in one of the largest such arrangements under the Trump administration's broader crackdown on immigration.
The deportees will be received within a year, with the first batch of 20 expected on Thursday, Liberia's Information Minister Jerolinmek Piah told reporters.
The 1,200 deportees will include Africans as well as nationals from North America, South America and the Caribbean, Piah said.
The Liberian minister did not say if the deportees expected in Liberia had such protection orders.
"The government of Liberia intends to provide the transferred persons with the necessary support to seek protection in Liberia and to be safe during their stay here."

title: Cleaner charged with sharing asylum seeker addresses in Thetford
summary:
A cleaner at a company that provides accommodation for asylum seekers has been charged with misconduct in public office over sharing the properties' addresses.
Houses in St John's Way, Bracken Road, Clover Way, Elm Road and Chester Way in Thetford, Norfolk, were targeted by crowds over three nights earlier this month.
James Jobson, 62, from Highlow Road, Costessey, near Norwich, works at Serco and appeared at Ipswich Magistrates' Court on Monday.
He was remanded in custody and will appear at Norwich Crown Court on 14 September.

title: People smuggler exposed by BBC investigation arrested and charged
summary:
A convicted people smuggler who was found by the BBC to be living in Leicestershire has been arrested and charged with immigration offences.
Last month, the BBC revealed he was now living in the UK.
The BBC has been told he was arrested on Tuesday near Uppingham in a joint operation led by the Midlands Criminal Financial Investigations team, with the support of Leicestershire Police.
He was charged by the Crown Prosecution Service and appeared at Leicester Magistrates' Court on Wednesday.
He has been remanded in custody and will next appear at Leicester Crown Court on 5 October.

title: Spain plans transfer of 500 migrant children from Ceuta to mainland
summary:

Madrid allocates Ceuta an ordinary reception capacity of 29 places, but shelters are now holding about 1,350 children, RTVE reported.

title: Palestinian refugee and two relatives drown off English coast
summary:
A girl is taken to hospital in critical condition in what PM Burnham calls a ‘terrible family tragedy’.
Three members of a Palestinian British family have drowned after entering the sea off England’s Sussex coast.
The father, Hossam al-Khawas, was a Palestinian refugee from the Rashidieh Camp in southern Lebanon near Tyre, the Press Association news agency reported.
“Hassan El-Khawas, 55, his partner, Zeina Alayn, 37, and their 14-year-old daughter, Sara El-Khawas were all confirmed deceased at the scene after being pulled from the water,” Sussex police said in a statement.
A fourth person – a younger girl who was also part of the family – was taken to hospital in a critical condition.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Vulnerable Texas Democrat Revealed Plan To Impose Mass Immigration In Unearthed Interview
summary:

In addition to taxpayer-funded facilities, housing, meals, and medical care, Gonzalez floated adding taxpayer-funded air travel to import migrants to their desired destination.

Gonzalez’s campaign did not immediately respond to a request for comment from the Daily Caller.
